translation_notes: prefixes: cvdo->cvdo, ndice->ndice, prov->prov, geo->geo, dowl->dowl, RDFS->rdfs (only the namespaces this region actually writes into a triple; rdf:type is Turtle's 'a' shorthand and needs no prefix). schema, vcard, bibtex, swc, nif, its, sdo, bibo, fabio, FOAF, virtrdf, ctr, XSD, DCTERMS, OWL are never used as a triple term in this region -- only passed to g.namespace_manager.bind(...) or (virtrdf, XSD) as plain Literal(...) datatype= arguments -- so they stay ordinary Python Namespace objects, no @prefix declared for them: an unused @prefix would be dead weight and (for the lowercase ones) a needless name collision.

STRATA IDIOM NOT USED, BY DESIGN: 'for @bindings in ...: +{ }' (the add_in_loop target idiom) does not fit here, matching the batch's own guidance for a body with heavy non-RDF logic entangled in the loop header. The double loop ('for row in reader: for heading in row:') is not itself a source of bindings rows: the inner loop walks a row's KEYS to decide, per heading, which predicate/datatype applies (six independent 'if heading == ...' branches computing metapredicate/metaobject, a nested zipcodes.matching() lookup with its own conditional add-block, and an emptiness guard) -- non-RDF branching that a bindings-producing iterable cannot express without inventing a row shape the original code never has. Kept both loops as plain Python 'for' (unchanged from original.py), and used the ordinary '@bindings {...}' declaration (a single-line mapping literal, assigned fresh right before each +{ }, not a loop form) wherever a +{ } needed more than one already-computed value (metapredicate+metaobject; the four zip-lookup values) -- '@bindings' + '+{ } with ?var' is still the most specific construction for those writes, just not through the loop-header spelling.

Three add-groups, three different needs, translated differently: (1) the zip/geo block (6 g.add() calls, lines 91-96) shares two different subjects (dice, then ndice[adm]) across six computed values -- '@bindings' holds the four literal/IRI values common to the first four adds, '?var' in +{ } pulls them, kept as TWO +{ } islands (not merged into one) because the subject changes; dice and ndice:{adm} themselves stay bare {expr}/prefixed-name interpolation since they are single already-known values, not values worth naming in a mapping. (2) the general row block (lines 104-106) merges the type-triple and the metapredicate/metaobject triple -- same subject dice, adjacent, unconditionally both-or-neither under one 'if' -- into a single '+{ dice a cvdo:ProductPurchasing ; ?p ?o }', with '@bindings {"p": metapredicate, "o": metaobject}' immediately above it (both values vary by heading, so binding them reads like the row they represent). (3) the provenance block (lines 109-112) is invariant except for the constant dice subject reused from above: no per-iteration values to bind, so kept as plain {expr} interpolation with no @bindings at all -- forcing bindings there would not be the most specific construction, just the most uniform-looking one.

ex:{?v} vs e<...{?v}>: adm (a two-letter ISO country code from zipcodes.matching(), e.g. 'US') is a plain identifier with no space or slash, so ndice:{adm} (bare local-part interpolation, immediate, not a bindings variable since adm is an ordinary already-known Python value at that point) concatenates safely; e<...> encoding was not needed and would just add a construction not exercised by real data here.

LdpyWarning 'prefixe declare = nom Python', CONFIRMED (INSTRUCTIONS.md 2bis): cvdo, ndice, prov, geo and dowl are each BOTH a declared @prefix (needed for the prefixed-name/variable terms above) AND a lowercase Python Namespace object kept unchanged for g.namespace_manager.bind(...) and the dynamic subscripts cvdo[strCamelCase] / ndice[adm] the original code also does. Verified empirically (see this region's own translated.ldpy transpile output) that the warning is diagnostic only: cvdo[strCamelCase], the bind() calls and cvdo:hasCountry-style prefixed names all resolve correctly side by side, because the collision the warning guards against ({cvdo:x} as a dict vs a set) never actually occurs in this file. Real trap, but a harmless one here -- reported per the batch instructions' 'un vrai piege du fichier, pas du bruit'.

Context shim (context_shim.py): pandas and collections.OrderedDict are re-exported as-is; repl() is copied verbatim from the same source file (dice-group/COVID19DS@7842845de5's toRdf.py, lines 128-129, defined AFTER handleFile() at module scope -- already bound by the time the real file calls handleFile() at its own bottom line 132). The CSV the region's own 'reader = pd.read_csv(...)' line reads (COVID19_INDEX_SAMPLE_....csv, literal relative filename, unchanged) is not in the source repository (a local dataset, never committed -- confirmed via the GitHub contents API: the directory holds only README and toRdf.py) and is reconstructed as a small, real 2-row fixture with the exact columns the code branches on (UPC, QTY, STORE_ZIP_CODE, NET_SALES, GROSS_SALES, DATE, plus one generic PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION column), including one row with several empty cells to exercise the 'row[heading] != ""' skip guard, and two real US zip codes (90210, 10001) so zipcodes.matching() returns genuine, verifiable geodata (both checked directly against the installed zipcodes package). zipcodes was on PyPI but absent from the venv; installed it (ordinary dependency, no native/network requirement -- ~/.venvs/ldpy/bin/pip install zipcodes).

Demo harness (see driver.py): handleFile() takes no argument, returns nothing, and mutates the module-level graph `g` through closure rather than a parameter -- entry='handleFile' mode only compares a call's return value, mutated args/kwargs and stdout, so it would see nothing and pass regardless of what the function actually built (a hollow green). Appended 'handleFile()' at module level, identically to both original.py and translated.ldpy (same pattern as examples/remove/DataDrivenCPS__acquirium__.../driver.py), and switched driver.py to entry=None so module-state comparison picks up `g` by name and checks it by graph isomorphism.

Sabotage-tested: in the general row block, rebinding the bindings so ?o resolves to {dice} instead of metaobject (so every heading's value-triple wrongly repeats the subject as the object) makes rdfeval check fail (graphs not isomorphic, 28 vs 28 triples -- same count, wrong edges); restored before finalising.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the nineteen `g.namespace_manager.bind(...)` calls become a `prefixes` dict and a `g.bind` loop. Graph.bind passes the same override=True/replace=False to namespace_manager.bind, and the dict keeps the order of the calls.

optimized.py: `rowNum` comes from `enumerate(reader, 1)`. dice is `ndice[f"{rowNum}_ProductPurchasingBehavior"]` once per row: re.sub on the digits of rowNum never matches an underscore, and resource is the same IRI as ndice. The heading loop is `row.items()`.

optimized.py: the five datatype overrides become a `datatypes` dict and the two predicate overrides a `predicates` dict, used with `.get(heading, default)`. The zip-code branch tests `heading == 'STORE_ZIP_CODE' and value != ""` and keeps `zipcodes.matching(...)[0]` in zipcodeInfo. The geometry literal is an f-string. The local `dice = None` goes. The provenance is written once per row, not once per heading (same graph).
optimized.py: the adds stay one call per triple. g is a module global inside a function, so `g += [...]` would need a `global g`, which a reviewer would reject.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: one `@prefix xsd:` at the top of the function body (the fixed header has none), and `@graph g`. The six zip-code triples are one `+{ }`, with the city, county and label as `{...}^^xsd:string` and the geometry as `f"POINT(...)"^^{virtrdf.Geometry}`. The two conditional triples and the four provenance triples are one `+{ }` each. The dicts hold `xsd:integer`, `cvdo:quantity` and other prefixed names. dice is `ndice:{rowNum}_ProductPurchasingBehavior`.
No exception to the symmetry rule. The added `@prefix xsd:` line pays for itself: five `Literal(..., datatype=XSD.x)` calls become `^^xsd:x`.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: URIRef and BNode are unused imports and go. The first `g = Graph()`, which the second one overwrites, and `resource` (unused, because dice is now `ndice[...]`) also go. The seventeen Namespace objects stay: the bind dict uses them.

optimized_header.ldpy: URIRef, BNode, XSD, RDF and RDFS go (the islands use a, rdfs: and xsd:). DCTERMS and OWL stay for the bind dict. The duplicate `g = Graph()` and `resource` also go. The six `@prefix` lines of the header are all used.
